josephus.author: Josephus

josephus.author: Josephus

philo.author: Philo
philo.summary: Philo explains why he understands the written laws to have been given in the wilderness before Israel settled in cities.
philo.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

philo.author: Philo
philo.summary: Philo distinguishes the ten principal laws, which he says God delivered directly, from particular laws communicated through Moses.
philo.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

philo.author: Philo
philo.summary: Philo describes the ten laws as delivered to the assembled nation and discusses their direct, singular form of address.
philo.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

philo.author: Philo
philo.summary: Philo presents the Ten Commandments as headings under which the more specific laws are organized, including Sabbath and festival laws.

philo.author: Philo

philo.author: Philo
philo.work: On the Life of Moses II
philo.summary: Philo retells the making of the golden calf during Moses' absence, Moses' intercession and descent, and the ensuing judgment.
philo.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: Jubilees frames its revelation with Moses ascending Sinai, receiving two stone tablets, and hearing of a covenant established there.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: The work anticipates Israel forsaking commandments, covenant festivals, Sabbaths, and sanctuary, followed by scattering and eventual return.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: The narrative says the angel of the presence is commanded to write for Moses and takes tablets containing the ordered divisions of law and testimony.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: Jubilees identifies the Sabbath as a sign, associates its observance with Israel, and gives an extended account of Sabbath obligations.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: Jubilees links the mountain covenant and its blood rite with an annual Feast of Weeks observance described as covenant renewal.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

jubilees.author: Jubilees
jubilees.summary: The closing chapter presents Sabbath and jubilee instructions as communicated to Moses at Sinai and lists Sabbath restrictions.
jubilees.notes: This passage is a later retelling or interpretation of biblical tradition, not independent evidence of the Sinai event.

detailSections.title: Covenant initiation
detailSections.summary: Israel arrives at Sinai. God proposes a covenant relationship, and the people answer that they will do what God has spoken.

detailSections.title: Covenant ratification
detailSections.summary: Moses reports the words and ordinances, records them, builds an altar, reads the covenant document, and applies covenant blood after the people affirm their response.

detailSections.title: Golden calf breach
detailSections.summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make and worship a calf. Moses breaks the tablets after descending and seeing the calf and dancing.

detailSections.title: Covenant renewal
detailSections.summary: Moses is commanded to cut two replacement tablets. Exodus 34 presents renewed covenant words and commands following the breach.
